::: {.subtitle}
Interactive tools for teaching viral evolution
:::

These are the materials I use in class. Both apps run entirely in your browser
— nothing to install, no account, and no server to log in to, so a whole class
can open them at once.

## Apps

::: {.resource}
### Within-host norovirus evolution
::: {.meta}
BIOL 463 · runs in the browser
:::

Follow a single patient with a prolonged norovirus GII.4 infection across nine
capsid sequences sampled over 111 days. Browse the alignment, read a
time-scaled phylogeny, fit the molecular clock, and compute dN/dS between any
two time points — then compare the within-host rate with the global
population-level rate for the same variant.

[Open the app](teaching/norovirus/){.btn-soft}
[Below on this page](#norovirus){.btn-ghost}
:::

::: {.resource}
### Molecular epidemiology of H3N2
::: {.meta}
BIOL 463 · runs in the browser
:::

Sixteen years of seasonal influenza: 313 HA sequences from the northern
hemisphere alongside 1,670 weeks of WHO sentinel surveillance. Explore the case
curves, the characteristically ladder-like HA phylogeny, the molecular clock,
and lineages through time — then overlay genetic diversity on the epidemic
curve.

[Open the app](teaching/h3n2/){.btn-soft}
[Below on this page](#h3n2){.btn-ghost}
:::

::: {.panel}
**First load takes a few seconds** — the page is fetching a small R environment
into your browser. After that everything is instant, and it keeps working
offline. Needs a current browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge).
:::

## Data and source

Everything behind both apps is open, so students can rerun the analyses in full
R and get the same numbers.

::: {.plain}
- **P33 capsid alignment** — 9 sequences, 1,620 nt, one prolonged infection
  [[FASTA](site/data/P33_capsid.fasta)]
- **Sydney 2012 capsid subsample** — 350 sequences sampled worldwide, 2011–2022
  [[FASTA](site/data/Sydney_2012_capsid_n350.fasta)]
- **H3N2 HA alignment** — 313 sequences, northern hemisphere, 2010–2026
  [[FASTA](site/data/H3N2_HA_northern_2010_2026.fasta)]
- **WHO sentinel surveillance** — weekly influenza counts by hemisphere
  [[CSV](site/data/WHO-H3N2-global-cases.csv)]
- **Apps and analysis scripts** — both Shiny apps plus the preparation scripts
  that do the phylogenetics
  [[GitHub](https://github.com/ldamodaran/ldamodaran.github.io)]
:::

::: {.panel}
**A note on the norovirus dates.** Sampling dates for patient P33 are shifted
to a placeholder year so that the real calendar dates are not published. The
intervals between samples — and therefore every rate in the app — are
unchanged.
:::

## How I use these in class

::: {.panel}
Students work through the tabs in order and answer the questions on the final
tab of each app. Each step is built from the one before it, so the apps are
designed to be followed start to finish rather than dipped into: the alignment
motivates the tree, the tree makes a rate measurable, and the rate sets up the
question of selection. The norovirus app is the within-host case, where
mutation and selection are observed directly; the H3N2 app is its
population-level counterpart. The question sets cross-reference each other.
:::
